faq.q: How do I use HJ Video Downloader?
faq.a: Open the home page, paste a video link, press Parse, choose MP4 or MP3 plus a quality, then Download and Save to device when it finishes. Separate several links with spaces for batch downloads.
Everything yt-dlp covers — 1000+ sites, including YouTube, Bilibili, Douyin, Kuaishou, Weibo, Xiaohongshu, Twitter/X, Instagram, TikTok, Vimeo, Twitch and SoundCloud.
Payments are not enabled yet. The free tier covers parsing and downloading; the pricing page only shows planned benefits.

faq.q: Can it summarize videos with no subtitles?
faq.a: No. The current version requires subtitles and says so clearly; speech-to-text is planned for a later release.

/summarize.heading: AI Summaries at a Glance

points: Reads subtitles only — usually done in 3-10 seconds

faq.q: What kind of video summarizes well?
faq.a: Spoken-word content: lectures, interviews, talks, podcasts and explainers. Purely visual walkthroughs lose too much.
Accuracy is capped by subtitle quality. Auto-generated captions mishear proper nouns, so verify anything you plan to act on.

faq.q: Does it download the video first?
faq.a: No. Only the subtitle track is read, which is why summarizing is far quicker than watching or downloading the file.

faq.q: Is an online tool or desktop software better?
faq.a: Occasional and cross-device use favours online tools; heavy batch work with fine control favours desktop software; extensions suit save-as-you-watch.

faq.q: Should new projects use yt-dlp or youtube-dl?
faq.a: Usually yt-dlp. It is the actively maintained fork, keeps up with platform changes, and supports concurrent fragments plus finer format selection.
